term_types.name: Key isolation mechanism
term_types.question: What mechanism isolates the key material from network-accessible components?
term_types.description: Specifies the hardware or logical mechanism that keeps keys separated from network-exposed processing, such as secure elements, enclaves, or HSMs.
values: trusted execution environment or secure enclave

term_types.name: Key distribution method across isolation boundary
term_types.question: How is key material or signed data moved between the isolated and connected environments?
term_types.description: Describes the channel used to carry keys, signatures, or transaction data across the isolation boundary.

term_types.name: Finality guarantee mode
term_types.question: Once a transaction is included, can it be reversed by any party, and under what condition?
term_types.description: Describes the form of finality a protocol provides: absolute, probabilistic with confirmation depth, or conditional on a quorum or synchrony assumption.

term_types.name: Key share cryptographic primitive
term_types.question: Which cryptographic primitive is used to split or share the signing key?
term_types.description: Distinguishes the mathematical scheme underlying the key split, such as Shamir secret sharing, threshold signatures, or MPC protocols.

values.value: physical point-of-sale or kiosk deployment in jurisdiction
values.definition: Crypto-asset services delivered through physical terminals, kiosks or ATMs located in the jurisdiction, creating a local nexus.

values.value: tokenized real-world asset in vault or escrow
values.definition: Backing asset is a physical or real-world item held in a vault, escrow account, or custodial store and represented one-to-one by an on-chain token.
Signing authority is split across parties via MPC or threshold signatures, with no single party holding a complete key, specifically for redeeming or transferring assets.
Succinct non-interactive argument of knowledge whose construction requires a trusted setup ceremony for common reference string generation.
Recovery is performed by a dedicated recovery key or escrowed key held separately from the owner keys and used to re-authorise or re-encrypt access.
Nodes are first filtered by a computed capability, credit, or trust score threshold, then selected randomly from the qualifying set.
Nodes are chosen to form a committee or endorse blocks according to an aggregated trust, credit, or evaluation score computed by peers.
Validators are chosen by votes or bids weighted by shares, tokens, or auction offers held by candidate nodes.
Cross-chain state or value is moved via a committee, notary group, or threshold signature attesting to source-chain events.
Assets are exchanged across chains using hashlocks and timelocks so that either both transfers complete or neither does.
Learns node or subgraph embeddings from transaction graphs with neural architectures such as GNNs, GAT, or attention models to classify addresses.
Ledger obtains external or cross-chain state via a dedicated oracle or relay that verifies source-chain data for the target chain.
Ledger applications that track goods, food, or pharmaceuticals across supply chain stages to verify origin and authenticity.
Ledger applications enabling prosumers and consumers to trade electricity directly, often via auctions or microgrid markets.
Participant identity is bound to ledger entries via decentralised identifiers anchored on the ledger and attested by verifiable credentials.
Correctness is established by interactive or automated proof assistants reasoning over the code's semantics with Hoare logic, invariants, or weakest preconditions.
A primary chain with one or more subsidiary chains that are anchored to or validated through the mainchain.

values.value: key-derivation from parent key or device-bound seed
values.definition: Signing authority is controlled by deriving child or wallet keys from a parent key, seed, or physically unclonable function response rather than storing a standalone key.
The signing key is held intact in one location without division.

values.value: Bitcoin script with transaction-chaining state machine
values.definition: Restricted base script whose expressiveness is extended by chaining transactions to emulate state machines or complex logic across multiple transactions.
